feat: add build_include support to Image for custom build context files

Adds a `build_include_paths` field and a `build_include(*file_paths)` method to the `Image` class. The method accepts one or more paths relative to the bento context root, appends them to the include list, and returns `self` to allow method chaining. These paths are propagated into the image build configuration and an `ImageInfo` dataclass field of the same name.

The Dockerfile template is updated to emit a `COPY` instruction for each entry in `build_include`, placing the files under `./src/<name>` in the image. The pip install step is adjusted to run with `./src` as its working directory and reference the requirements file via an absolute `$BENTO_PATH`-prefixed path.

Wheel handling is also revised: wheels are no longer moved from their source location into a separate subdirectory before packaging. Instead, references to the wheels path are updated throughout to point directly at `src/wheels`, and the URL pattern check for local wheel links is extended to match both the old `/env/python/wheels` path and the new `/src/wheels` path. When a wheels directory is present, `"wheels"` is automatically appended to `build_include_paths`.

feat: add broker_pool_acquire_timeout config option and fix eta=now routing

A new `broker_pool_acquire_timeout` configuration option (float, default `None`) is added to the broker namespace. When set, this value is passed to the connection pool's acquire call, limiting how long task dispatch will block waiting for an available connection. When the pool limit is exceeded within the specified timeout, a `LimitExceeded` exception is now caught and re-raised as `OperationalError`.

The delayed-delivery routing logic is also corrected so that it only evaluates quorum queue detection when `eta` or `countdown` is actually provided. Previously the driver type was unconditionally queried. Additionally, when `eta` resolves to the current time, the resulting `countdown` of zero (falsy) no longer triggers delayed exchange routing, leaving the original queue and routing key unchanged.

Unit tests cover the eta-equals-now edge case and verify that the configured timeout value is forwarded to the pool acquire call. Integration tests confirm that normal dispatch works with a timeout set, that `None` (block indefinitely) remains the default behavior, and that concurrent dispatch under a configured timeout completes without deadlock.

feat: expose time_limit and soft_time_limit as first-class Context attributes

`Context` now declares `time_limit` and `soft_time_limit` as explicit class-level attributes (defaulting to `None`). Whenever `Context.update()` receives a `timelimit` key — regardless of whether the argument is a mapping, an iterable of pairs, or a keyword argument — the method unpacks the first two elements of the value into those attributes. An O(1) identity-check on a module-level sentinel detects whether `timelimit` changed, avoiding any pre-scan of the input.

`Task` gains two additional app-config bindings so that `task_time_limit` and `task_soft_time_limit` configuration values propagate to `time_limit` and `soft_time_limit` on the task class. The request dict assembled during dispatch now always includes a `timelimit` entry, ensuring the unpacking path is exercised for both declaratively configured tasks and those whose limits are supplied at call time via `apply_async`.

New unit tests cover all accepted `dict.update()` input forms (plain dict, list of pairs, `dict.items()`, and kwargs), as well as the `None` / invalid-value clearing behaviour. Integration tests verify that `task.request.time_limit` and `task.request.soft_time_limit` are correctly `None` when no limits are configured, match values supplied to `apply_async`, and reflect limits declared at the task class level.

feat: add credential provider support to Redis backend

A new configuration option `redis_backend_credential_provider` is introduced for the Redis backend. It accepts either a dotted-string class path or a direct instance of a `redis.CredentialProvider` subclass. When a string is supplied, the class is resolved and instantiated at connection setup time.

When a credential provider is active, the `username` and `password` keys are automatically removed from the connection parameters to avoid conflicts. Passing a value that is neither a valid string path to a `CredentialProvider` subclass nor an actual `CredentialProvider` instance raises a `ValueError`. The same provider resolution logic is also applied when the credential provider is supplied as a query parameter in the connection URL.

Tests cover string-based class resolution, direct instance injection, an invalid class path raising `ImportError`, and a non-conforming object raising `ValueError`. Additional test dependencies for Azure blob storage and gevent extras are included in the test requirements.

Title: StreamingResponse doc example needs correction

Body:
[`StreamingResponse` docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/custom-response/?h=responses#streamingresponse) state:

> Takes an async generator or a normal generator/iterator

However based on [linked reference; provenance retained by controller] `async` generetors need something `await`ed to work:

```py
import asyncio
from time import sleep
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

app = FastAPI()

async def fake_video_streamer():
    for i in range(10):
        sleep(0.1)
        yield b"some fake video bytes"
        # await asyncio.sleep(0)  # <-- uncomment to fix example

@app.get("/")
async def main():
    """
    this is as per
    https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/custom-response/?h=responses#streamingresponse
    but does not to work (blocks for 1 sec, then returns all chunks at once):
      curl -sNo- localhost:8000
      wget -qO- localhost:8000
    """
    return StreamingResponse(fake_video_streamer())
```

- `uvicorn==0.40.0`
- `fastapi==0.128.0`
